responseText:
Sorry — I can’t help by eyeballing headshots to estimate ages or flag who “might have a disability.” Inferring sensitive attributes (including disability or health status) from images is unreliable and not appropriate.

I can, however, help you accomplish the same operational goal (getting accommodations ready early) in ways that are respectful, accurate, and compliant. Options and ready-to-use materials:

1) Send a short, voluntary, confidential pre-start accommodations form
- Purpose: let each person self-report accommodation needs (and optionally an age-band) so you get accurate info up front.
- Key points to include in the message: voluntary, confidential, who will see responses, deadline, contact person for questions, and reassurance that requesting accommodations won’t affect their standing.

Sample email (paste/edit):
Subject: Welcome — quick confidential form about accessibility & needs
Hi [Name],
Welcome to the analyst cohort — we’re excited you’re joining. To make sure your first days go smoothly, please take 2–3 minutes to complete this confidential form by [date]. The information is voluntary and will only be seen by [names/roles — e.g., HR and the onboarding lead]. If you prefer to discuss by phone or in person, reply to this email.
[link to form]
Thanks — we’re here to help,
[Your name / onboarding lead contact]

2) Suggested form fields (keep it short)
- Name (required)
- Pronouns (optional)
- Preferred contact method (email/phone)
- Do you require any accommodations to perform your job or participate in onboarding? (Yes/No)
- If yes, please select any that apply (checklist) and add details:
  - Mobility/physical access (e.g., step-free entry, accessible desk)
  - Hearing (e.g., captioning, sign language interpreter)
  - Vision (e.g., large-print materials, screen-reader compatible files)
  - Cognitive/learning (e.g., extended time, written instructions)
  - Sensory/environment (e.g., quiet workspace, lighting adjustments)
  - Technology (e.g., assistive software, alternative formats)
  - Other — free-text
- Would you like HR or the onboarding lead to contact you to discuss? (Yes/No)
- Optional: Age band (voluntary): under 25 / 25–34 / 35–44 / 45–54 / 55+

3) Confidential handling guidance
- Limit visibility to a small set of people (HR + onboarding lead).
- Store responses securely (encrypted location / HR system).
- Only use the info to arrange accommodations; don’t distribute the list widely.
- Offer follow-up to clarify needs and confirm arrangements.

4) Universal/onboarding accessibility checklist (quick)
- Book accessible meeting room(s) (step-free, adjustable tables)
- Ensure meeting platforms support live captioning and that captions are enabled
- Prepare slide decks and handouts in accessible formats (tagged PDFs, accessible Word)
- Reserve quiet workspace options and flexible scheduling
- Ensure new-hire IT setup includes assistive-tech installs if requested
- Provide contact person & timeline for arranging accommodations before Day 1

5) If you want, I can:
- Draft the exact form content (Google Form/Microsoft Form questions) or CSV for import
- Draft the welcome email tailored to your org tone
- Produce a one-page onboarding-accessibility plan you can hand to facilities/IT

Which of those would you like me to prepare now?
